references.text: Deuteronomy repeats the clean and unclean animals, including locusts as permitted food.
John the Baptist ate locusts and wild honey, showing that locusts were considered clean food according to Mosaic Law.
Mark confirms that John the Baptist ate locusts, in agreement with the permitted insects mentioned in Leviticus.
The plague of locusts in Egypt highlights the significance of locusts in a biblical context and their connection to the history of the Israelites.
Joel mentions different types of locusts, showing the variety of locust species known in ancient Israel.
